record.context_brief: Unique continuation along a level surface for elliptic equations.
record.original_question: Let Omega be a connected open subset of R^n with n >= 2. Let A = A(x) be a symmetric matrix-valued coefficient field such that the elliptic equation div(A grad u) = 0 in Omega satisfies the uniform ellipticity bounds K^(-1)|xi|^2 <= A(x)xi·xi <= K|xi|^2 for all x, xi in R^n and the Lipschitz bound |A(x) - A(y)| <= E|x - y| for all x, y in R^n. Let u and v be two nonconstant solutions of div(A grad w) = 0 in Omega, let S be a connected smooth hypersurface of dimension n-1 contained in Omega, and let Sigma be an open proper subset of S. If u = 0 on all of S and v = 0 on Sigma, must v also vanish on all of S?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a connected open set. Let $A : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ be a symmetric matrix-valued coefficient field satisfying, for some constants $K \geq 1$ and $E \geq 0$, the uniform ellipticity bounds
$$K^{-1}|\xi|^2 \leq A(x)\xi \cdot \xi \leq K|\xi|^2 \qquad \text{for all } x,\xi \in \mathbb{R}^n,$$
and the Lipschitz bound
$$|A(x) - A(y)| \leq E|x-y| \qquad \text{for all } x,y \in \mathbb{R}^n.$$
Consider the elliptic equation
$$\operatorname{div}(A(x)\nabla w) = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega.$$
Let $u$ and $v$ be two nonconstant (weak) solutions of this equation in $\Omega$. Let $S \subset \Omega$ be a connected smooth hypersurface of dimension $n-1$, and let $\Sigma$ be an open proper subset of $S$. Suppose that $u \equiv 0$ on $S$ and $v \equiv 0$ on $\Sigma$.

Must it then follow that $v \equiv 0$ on all of $S$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem (Problem 2.1, "Unique continuation along level surfaces") in a 2020 collection of open problems by G. Alessandrini. A targeted web search did not uncover any subsequent publication resolving the question for Lipschitz elliptic coefficients in dimension n ≥ 2, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Collection of unsolved problems the author encountered throughout his career, including Problem 2.1 on unique continuation along level surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open problem in this 2020 collection.

status_evidence.title: Unique Continuation Property for the Level Set Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies unique continuation properties related to level sets, but does not resolve the divergence-form question with Lipschitz coefficients posed here.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature exists on level-set unique continuation, but does not settle this specific question.
